use_when: To collect short text such as a name, email, or phone number
Form Input for forms with a label and helper text
Text Input for longer answers like notes or messages
Search to let people look up books or content
When input needs clear success or error feedback

dont_use_when.when: When there are only a few fixed choices.
To display information that can't be edited.
For dates or numbers where a picker is easier.

best_practice: Show a label in forms. Don't use the placeholder as a replacement for it.
Keep the placeholder as a short example, not an instruction.
Use helper text to explain the format before people type, and error text to explain how to fix a problem after.

variant_intent.type=Form Input: Figma: forms with a label and helper text.
variant_intent.type=Text Input: Figma: longer answers like notes or messages.
variant_intent.type=Search Input: Figma: Search, to let people look up books or content.
variant_intent.type=Search Input with Button: Renders the search input with a button (code).
variant_intent.state=Success: Figma: Success tint; needs helper text, and ideally an icon, to say what happened.
variant_intent.state=Error: Figma: Error tint; needs helper text, and ideally an icon, to say what happened. Code also sets aria-invalid.
variant_intent.state=Disable: Disables the control. Figma: disabled fields are skipped by the keyboard, so do not use them for important information.

a11y.fact: The label is a <label> tied to the control with htmlFor.
The Error state sets aria-invalid on the control.
The control points at its helper text with aria-describedby.
When the label is hidden the control gets an aria-label.
Search types are wrapped in role="search".
The Disable state disables the control natively.
